answer: Resist Sybils with proof of sustained service: standing grows only while an identity runs a public service real peers actually use, like an ember that must be tended to stay lit. Random probes at unpredictable hours check the service is genuinely up, and an idle service in the tundra of inactivity sheds standing fast, so bought or copied identities starve. An oasis of real usage cannot be faked by clones that serve nobody: a farmer must keep thousands of live services running around the clock, each with its own users, paying full cost per fake, which makes mass fakery unprofitable.
